title: SceneWeave: Audience-Guided Scene Exploration for Dramatic Adaptation
abstract: arXiv:2610.21737v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Adapting prose into a script requires transforming narration and inner experience into scenes that convey relationships and psychological contradictions. Planning specifies intended effects but leaves their realization in dialogue and action unresolved. Drawing on screenwriters' accounts of revising scenes and their connections to the surrounding work, we present SceneWeave, which uses alternative scene drafts to revise the adaptation as a whole. It writes contrasting treatments of a focal scene, compares the interactions they create, and revises characterization, preceding preparation, subsequent development, and scene order before generating the complete script. The central contribution is to use actual scene writing to inform adaptation decisions and propagate their consequences across the work. translated_title: SceneWeave：面向戏剧改编的观众引导式场景探索
translated_abstract: 将散文改编成剧本需要把叙述和内心体验转化为能够传达人物关系与心理矛盾的场景。规划虽明确了预期效果，却未解决如何在对话与动作中实现这些效果。借鉴编剧关于修改场景及其与整体作品关联的经验，我们提出了SceneWeave，该方法利用备选场景草稿对改编进行整体修订。它为焦点场景撰写多种对比性处理方案，比较各方案所产生的人物互动，并在生成完整剧本之前，修订人物塑造、前期铺垫、后续发展以及场景顺序。其核心贡献在于利用实际的场景写作来指导改编决策，并将其后果传播至整个作品。我们还开发了一个面向任务的专业写作模型和一个用于比较剧本草稿的人类偏好模型。该写作模型从改编（数据中学习……）
tldr: SceneWeave通过为焦点场景撰写多种对比性草稿并比较其效果，将实际场景写作反馈用于指导戏剧改编决策，并将修改影响传播至全剧的人物塑造、情节铺垫、后续发展与场景顺序。
en_tdlr: SceneWeave uses contrasting drafts of focal scenes to inform adaptation decisions and propagate their consequences across characterization, setup, development, and scene order for holistic dramatic adaptation.
